external_entities.description: The external identity provider used for customer authentication.

external_entities.source_excerpt: The analytics team, a group of internal analysts

external_entities.name: Support administrator
external_entities.description: A staff support administrator using the administrative functions of the Orders API.

processes.name: CloudFront
processes.description: Serves the React single-page web app to the public internet and has AWS WAF request limiting applied.
processes.source_excerpt: CloudFront serves it to the public internet over HTTPS with TLS 1.3

processes.name: React single-page web app
processes.description: A publicly loadable React single-page web application that calls the internal Orders API.
processes.source_excerpt: The web app calls an internal Orders API in our AWS VPC over HTTPS

processes.name: Orders API
processes.description: An internal API that authenticates requests, applies customer rate limits, accesses orders, handles support administration, and sends payment authorisation.
processes.source_excerpt: The Orders API reads and writes a Postgres database in a private subnet

processes.name: Nightly batch job
processes.description: A nightly job that reads at most one day of orders and writes summaries to S3.
processes.source_excerpt: A nightly batch job in the VPC reads at most one day of orders

processes.name: Athena
processes.description: The query service used by analysts to query the analytics bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The analytics team, a group of internal analysts, query that bucket through Athena

processes.name: Admin console
processes.description: The administrative console used to perform support actions on the Orders API.
processes.source_excerpt: Support administrators are staff who use an admin console on the Orders API

processes.name: AWS WAF
processes.description: A web application firewall on CloudFront that limits each client to 2,000 requests per five minutes.
processes.source_excerpt: AWS WAF on CloudFront limits each client to 2,000 requests per five minutes

data_stores.name: Postgres database
data_stores.description: The database holding customer names, delivery addresses, phone numbers, and order history.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It holds customer names, delivery addresses, phone numbers, and order history

data_stores.name: Database snapshots
data_stores.description: Snapshots of the Orders database that the platform team can copy or restore.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Only the platform team can copy or restore the database snapshots

data_stores.name: KMS-encrypted S3 bucket
data_stores.description: An S3 bucket containing summaries written by the nightly batch job and queried through Athena.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes summaries over HTTPS, with its own IAM role, to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket

data_stores.name: CloudWatch Logs audit log
data_stores.description: An audit log receiving each support administrator action; administrators cannot change it.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a KMS- encrypted CloudWatch Logs audit log that administrators cannot change

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Customer sign-in to the Auth0 identity provider.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers sign in to our Auth0 identity provider over HTTPS with TLS 1.3, using a password and MFA.

data_flows.name: load app
data_flows.description: Customer loads the publicly available React single-page web app from CloudFront.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Anyone can load our React single-page web app without signing in; CloudFront serves it to the public internet over HTTPS with TLS 1.3.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The web app calls the Orders API with an Auth0 OAuth2 bearer token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web app calls an internal Orders API in our AWS VPC over HTTPS. Every call carries an Auth0 OAuth2 bearer token

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: Orders API reads and writes order data in the Postgres database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The Orders API reads and writes a Postgres database in a private subnet over TLS
data_flows.data_description: Customer names, delivery addresses, phone numbers, and order history

data_flows.name: payment authorisation
data_flows.description: Orders API sends payment authorisation to Stripe.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Payment authorisation goes to Stripe over HTTPS with a secret API key

data_flows.name: read orders
data_flows.description: Nightly batch job reads at most one day of orders using a read-only database role.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A nightly batch job in the VPC reads at most one day of orders over TLS with a read-only database role.
data_flows.data_description: At most one day of orders

data_flows.name: write summaries
data_flows.description: Nightly batch job writes summaries to the KMS-encrypted S3 bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes summaries over HTTPS, with its own IAM role, to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket.

data_flows.name: query bucket
data_flows.description: Analytics team queries the analytics bucket through Athena.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The analytics team, a group of internal analysts, query that bucket through Athena

data_flows.name: read summaries
data_flows.description: Athena reads the analytics bucket over TLS using read-only IAM roles.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Athena, which reads it over TLS, with read- only IAM roles

data_flows.name: administer orders
data_flows.description: Support administrators use the Orders API to refund orders, edit delivery addresses, and look up order history.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Through it they refund orders, edit delivery addresses, and look up order history.
data_flows.data_description: Refunds, delivery addresses, and order history

data_flows.name: write audit actions
data_flows.description: Orders API writes each support administrator action to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API writes each action over HTTPS, with its IAM role, to a KMS- encrypted CloudWatch Logs audit log

data_flows.name: copy or restore snapshots
data_flows.description: Platform team copies or restores database snapshots.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Only the platform team can copy or restore the database snapshots
data_flows.authentication: IAM roles with SSO and MFA

data_flows.name: copy or restore bucket
data_flows.description: Platform team copies or restores the S3 bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Only the platform team can copy or restore the database snapshots, the bucket and the audit log, through IAM roles with SSO and MFA over HTTPS.
data_flows.authentication: IAM roles with SSO and MFA

data_flows.name: copy or restore audit log
data_flows.description: Platform team copies or restores the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Only the platform team can copy or restore the database snapshots, the bucket and the audit log, through IAM roles with SSO and MFA over HTTPS.
data_flows.authentication: IAM roles with SSO and MFA

assumptions.assumption: The customer is reachable from and located in the public internet zone for the described public application access.
assumptions.basis: The customer loads the application from the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The customer carries personally identifying information and authentication credentials while signing in and using the system.
assumptions.basis: Customers provide a password and MFA and are customers of the service.

assumptions.assumption: CloudFront is internet-facing because it serves the application to the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The text says CloudFront serves the application to the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The React single-page web app is internet-facing because anyone can load it without signing in.
assumptions.basis: The text says anyone can load the app without signing in.

assumptions.assumption: The React single-page web app holds or handles bearer credentials and order-related data because it calls the Orders API with a bearer token.
assumptions.basis: The app calls the API and every call carries an Auth0 OAuth2 bearer token.

assumptions.assumption: The Orders API handles financial data because it performs payment authorisation and refunds orders.
assumptions.basis: Payment authorisation goes to Stripe and support administrators can refund orders.

assumptions.assumption: The nightly batch job handles personally identifying information because it reads orders containing customer information.
assumptions.basis: The job reads orders, and the database holds customer names, addresses, phone numbers, and order history.

assumptions.assumption: The KMS-encrypted S3 bucket contains personally identifying information because its summaries are produced from orders containing customer information.
assumptions.basis: The batch job reads orders and writes summaries to the bucket.

assumptions.assumption: The analytics team handles personally identifying and business-critical data because it queries the analytics summaries derived from orders.
assumptions.basis: The analytics team queries the bucket containing order summaries.

assumptions.assumption: The CloudWatch Logs audit log contains personally identifying, financial, and business-critical data because it records support actions involving refunds, delivery addresses, and order history.
assumptions.basis: The API writes each support administrator action to the audit log.

assumptions.assumption: The support administrator handles personally identifying, financial, and business-critical data because the administrator refunds orders, edits delivery addresses, and looks up order history.
assumptions.basis: The described administrative actions involve refunds, delivery addresses, and order history.

assumptions.assumption: The platform team handles business-critical data because it can copy or restore database snapshots, the bucket, and the audit log.
assumptions.basis: The platform team has copy and restore access to the named system stores.

assumptions.assumption: The database snapshots contain the same personally identifying and business-critical data as the database they snapshot.
assumptions.basis: The snapshots are described as database snapshots, and the database holds customer information and order history.

assumptions.assumption: The database snapshots are confidential because they contain customer information and order history.
assumptions.basis: The snapshots represent a database holding names, addresses, phone numbers, and order history.

assumptions.assumption: The Postgres database is confidential because it holds customer names, delivery addresses, phone numbers, and order history.
assumptions.basis: Those contents are explicitly stated.

assumptions.assumption: The KMS-encrypted S3 bucket is confidential because it holds summaries derived from customer orders.
assumptions.basis: The bucket stores summaries written from order data.

assumptions.assumption: The CloudWatch Logs audit log is confidential because it records actions involving customer, order, address, and refund information.
assumptions.basis: The log records each described support administrator action.

assumptions.assumption: The database snapshot, bucket, and audit-log administration flows are read-write because copy and restore require both reading and writing.
assumptions.basis: The text explicitly says copy or restore.

assumptions.assumption: The bucket copy or restore flow is read-write because copy and restore require both reading and writing.
assumptions.basis: The text explicitly says copy or restore.

assumptions.assumption: The audit-log copy or restore flow is read-write because copy and restore require both reading and writing.
assumptions.basis: The text explicitly says copy or restore.
